power_of_two_scaling.row_rule: Multiply complete stored row and RHS by a positive exact2^k; keep sense. Reject if any finite nonzero transformed value is nonrepresentable, zero, overflowed or rounded.
power_of_two_scaling.column_rule: For continuous columns only let originalx=2^k*newz; multiply that column and objective by2^k, divide both finite bounds by2^k. Integer/binary columns keep k=0; global rho k=0 keeps original P1 coefficient. Exact real inverse required.
power_of_two_scaling.arithmetic_rule: Independently compare every resulting binary64 value to Fraction(original)*2^k (or divided bounds). No decimal reconstruction, threshold pruning, subnormal rounding or zeroing. Infinity bounds retain signs.
power_of_two_scaling.inverse_rule: A mapped native float must equal the exact rational inverse; reject a packet with underflow/rounding rather than repair or clip it.
power_of_two_scaling.native_rule: Even mathematically exact binary64 shifts may create coefficients the backend omits. Future actual CSR/RHS/sense/objective/type/bound readback must match exactly before any optimization.
power_of_two_scaling.matrix_size: Rows/columns/binaries/NNZ and structural graph unchanged. Scaling offers no structural fill reduction proof; current internalScaleFlag2 stays unchanged.
